{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for frontend teams:
1) Scope: apply changes to every UI surface and client-side module that reads or displays entries (single-entry views, lists, cards, tooltips, exports, client caches). Do not change server contracts yourself.
2) Remove fallback-reading of title: locate all code paths that read entry.title as a fallback when entry.name is missing (templates, components, render helpers, selectors, formatters). Remove the fallback so the UI consumes and displays only entry.name. After change, code should reference only entry.name for display and identification.
3) Avoid sending title: audit code that constructs request payloads (create/update) and ensure no client code includes a title property. If existing form state or legacy utilities may populate title, explicitly delete title from the outgoing payload before sending (e.g., delete payload.title or construct payload with explicit allowed fields: name, description, id, owner_id, created_at as applicable).
4) Error handling: ensure the UI handles server validation errors (HTTP 422). Add or keep a user-facing validation message for 422 responses caused by unexpected fields; verify that submitting a payload that includes title results in a surfaced 422 message and no silent failures.
5) Tests: add/adjust automated tests (unit/integration/e2e) to assert that:
   - UI always renders entry.name and never relies on entry.title.
   - Requests sent by the client do not include title.
   - Submitting a payload that includes title yields a 422 response and the UI surfaces the error.
6) Backward compatibility: do not attempt to read a title from any server response; code must tolerate responses that simply lack the title property. Do not change client-side storage schema names unless coordinated.
7) Docs and code comments: update client-side docs/comments to note that title is not part of the public response and should not be used.
8) Deploy checklist: run full test suite, smoke-test all entry display screens, verify no console errors due to removed fallback, and verify that creating/updating entries (without title) behaves as before."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for backend teams:
1) Scope: apply to every public API surface that returns entry objects (all REST endpoints, GraphQL types, RPC responses, and any HTTP responses consumed by third parties). Do not change the database schema or column names.
2) Remove title from responses: update serializers/DTOs/response mappers to omit the title property from all outgoing public responses for entry objects. Ensure response payloads still include name, description, id, owner_id, created_at and any other previously public fields unchanged.
3) Preserve DB and internal usage: do not rename or remove the title column in the database. Internal services or background jobs that reference the DB field may continue to use it; only the public response layer must stop exposing it.
4) Request validation: add explicit validation that rejects client requests that include a title field. If an incoming request body contains a title property, respond with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity (same 422 behavior as before). Ensure the error payload follows the existing error format for validation errors.
5) API schema/docs: update OpenAPI/GraphQL/schema documentation to remove title from response types and to mark title as forbidden in request schemas (or ensure request schema does not accept title). Clearly document that title is internal-only and not returned publicly.
6) Tests: add/adjust automated tests to assert:
   - All GET/list and GET/item responses for entries do not contain a title field and still contain name, description, id, owner_id, created_at unchanged.
   - Submitting a POST/PATCH/PUT request that includes a title in the payload returns HTTP 422 and does not change the stored DB record.
   - Internal persistence of title (DB column) remains unchanged after API operations.
7) Backward compatibility & logging: ensure logs, monitoring, and any audit exports that are considered internal may still include the DB title as needed, but do not leak title into public response logs or external monitoring exports.
8) Deployment & rollout: deploy serializer/validator changes together so responses stop exposing title at the same time request validation rejecting title is active. Run the test suite and smoke tests for all entry endpoints to confirm acceptance criteria:
   - Responses: title absent; name present.
   - Requests with title: return 422.
   - Database schema and fields description/id/owner_id/created_at unchanged.
9) Coordination note: do not make unilateral decisions about which endpoints are "public" vs "internal" — apply to any endpoint previously documented/consumed as public. If an endpoint is truly internal-only and must continue returning title, explicitly list it in a separate change request; do not assume exceptions."

  }
}
